_note: PLACEHOLDER TIMES: even split, not the real take. Let the vision cuts (make_lesson.ps1 -NoSpeech) find the real ones with this list as the prior, or retime by hand. check_type is for people: the CLI treats a step as manual when check_question is "manual". Needs only a hub quick release, a rim brake, spokes, tire, valve, and a rag.

steps.title: Squeeze the front brake and watch the pads meet the rim
steps.common_mistake: Squeeze the lever once before you start, so you know how the brake felt.

steps.title: Flip the quick release lever open and unwind the nut three turns
steps.check_question: Is the quick release lever swung open, standing out away from the fork blade?
steps.common_mistake: Flip the lever open first; do not unscrew it like a nut.

steps.title: Lift the front of the bike and drop the wheel out
steps.check_question: Are both fork ends empty, with no wheel between the fork blades?
steps.common_mistake: Lift the bike and let the wheel drop straight down out of the fork.

steps.title: Pull the skewer out and check both springs sit narrow end inward
steps.check_question: Is the skewer pulled out of the wheel, held or lying apart from the hub?
steps.common_mistake: Keep both springs; each one points its narrow end toward the hub.

steps.title: Wipe the braking surface of the rim all the way round
steps.check_question: Is a cloth pressed against the rim edge of a wheel held off the bike?
steps.common_mistake: Wipe the flat metal track the pads touch, not the tire.

steps.title: Pinch pairs of spokes around the wheel to find a loose one
steps.check_question: Is a hand pinching two spokes together on a wheel held off the bike?
steps.common_mistake: Squeeze two spokes at a time; a loose one gives more than its neighbors.

steps.title: Turn the wheel and look along the tire for cuts and glass, then check the valve stands straight
steps.common_mistake: Turn the wheel a full circle; look at the tread and both sidewalls.

steps.title: Slide the skewer back through the hub, lever on the left, springs narrow end in
steps.check_question: Is the skewer through the hub with its lever on one side of the wheel and the nut on the other?
steps.common_mistake: The lever goes on the left side of the bike, away from the chain.

steps.title: Lower the fork onto the axle so it seats in both slots
steps.check_question: Is the axle seated all the way into the slots of both fork ends, with the wheel centered between the fork blades?
steps.common_mistake: Press the bike down so the axle reaches the top of both slots.

steps.title: Snug the nut, then close the lever flat along the fork blade
steps.check_question: Is the quick release lever closed, lying flat along the fork blade and pointing up or back?
steps.common_mistake: Fold the lever back along the fork. A lever pointing forward can catch on something and open.

steps.title: Squeeze the brake and spin the wheel to check it runs clear of the pads
steps.check_question: Is a hand squeezing the brake lever on the handlebar with the wheel in the fork?
steps.common_mistake: Squeeze the brake once and spin the wheel before you ride.

safety: The quick release lever must be fully closed and flat along the fork before riding
The axle must sit at the top of both fork slots before closing the lever
Squeeze the brake and spin the wheel to test it before riding
